intro.text: Dusk over the Wayfarer's Chapel. The great bell is tolling — though no rope has been pulled in three nights.
Again. Nobody in the belfry, nobody on the rope, and still it rings. Father Aldous, you can't keep telling me it's the wind.
I stopped telling you that on the second night, Mu. Come here. It is time you heard what your bell-ringing was truly for.
Seven Silent Bells lie buried across the old world. Their echoes hold back the Long Silence — a hush that swallows names, then memories, then the living.
The first Bell has begun to crack, beneath the Old Town of Edinburgh. Take the Tolling Blade — the iron clapper of this very chapel's bell, reforged. It answers to you alone.
Alone? I've never been farther than the river.
Then it is well you will not be alone. A stonemason named Isolde waits by the north pews. She knows those vaults better than any map.

aldous_pre.text: Speak with Isolde, near the pews. The vaults of Edinburgh are no place to walk blind.
Move with WASD or arrows. Space strikes with the Tolling Blade, E speaks and opens, Q shifts form once the chapel's relics answer you.

isolde_meet.text: So you're the bell-boy. Isolde Marsh. I cut stone for the Old Town — and for three months I've been trying to cut my way into those vaults.
My brother Tomas went down with a lantern and a chisel to mend a collapsed arch. The arch got mended. He didn't come back up.
Your bells ring and the walls under my city hum back. If that's connected, then I'm coming with you. Don't argue — I'm very stubborn and I carry a hammer.
I wasn't going to argue. I was going to ask you to stay behind me when the rats come.

aldous_ready.text: The archway to the east leads north, to the Old Town. Go with God, and with Isolde.

aldous_after.text: The first Bell is mended. I felt it from here — the silence drew back a step.
A scholar named Corvin writes to me from Prague. He says the second Bell lies in the ossuary under an astronomical clock. The road there is not yet lit... but it will be.

portal_alone.text: I shouldn't go down there alone. Isolde was waiting by the north pews.

portal_done.text: The Edinburgh road lies quiet behind you. The way to Prague is not yet lit.
— To be continued in Chapter II: Prague, the Ossuary Clock —

worldmap.text: A map of the Silent Bells, inked in Aldous's careful hand.
I. Edinburgh — the South Bridge Vaults.  II. Prague — the Ossuary Clock.  III. Transylvania — the Hollow Keep.
IV. Paris — the Catacombs.  V. Whitby — the Drowned Abbey.  VI. Venice — the Sunken Palazzo.  VII. Rome — the Last Crypt.

vault_enter.text: Smell that? Damp lime and old iron. These vaults were sealed up and forgotten two hundred years ago.
Something down here is ringing in time with my bell.
Then follow the sound, and watch your feet. There'll be a key somewhere — the old merchants locked everything.

vault_key.text: You found an old iron key. Locked doors (E) will yield to it.

vault_locked.text: Locked tight. There must be a key somewhere in these vaults.

vault_puzzle.text: A floor plate, and a dressed stone block. Push the block onto the plate and the old gate should lift.
Wedge it in a corner and you'll have to press R to reset the stones.

vault_shrine_hint.text: There's a shrine at the back of the chamber. It's... humming.

shrine.text: A cracked bell-shaped shrine. As Mu's hand touches it, a cold voice, like a bell heard through water, whispers a name that isn't his.
You are not the first to be called, ringer. Take the Wraith's Echo. Wear the shade, and iron will not hold you.
Wraith Form unlocked! Press Q to shift. In this form you are swift and can slip through iron bars — but your strikes are weak.

shrine_after.text: The shrine's cold light mends your wounds.

vault_bars.text: Iron bars, and the sound is coming from just beyond them. I can't squeeze through those.
No. But I think the shade can. Q to shift form, then walk through — and shift back before the fight.

warden_defeated.text: The Hollow Warden collapses into dust. The cracked Bell above falls silent, its echo mended.
...Mu. Look at the lantern. The handle's wrapped in my mother's blue thread. That's Tomas's.
He stayed to guard it. Even after he was gone, he guarded it. Stubborn. Just like me.
Don't be. He's resting now. And the city above has one less ghost in its walls. I'm coming to the next Bell — I want to know what's driving this.
The first Silent Bell is mended. A portal of pale light opens in the hall.

aldous_prague.text: Two bells mended, and the old road holding. You have both grown, you know. Not taller — quieter, in the way that matters.
Go carefully. Whatever is winding the Bells, it is patient, and patience is the cruelest kind of cold.

portal_done2.text: The portal hums, and along the chapel's north wall five Echo Gates glimmer — each a door into the place where a legend still walks.
Chapter III's roads are not yet lit, but the Echoes can be faced now. Walk the northern gates in order.

isolde_gone.text: Isolde went north at dawn, to the cottage and her mother's loom. She left her thanks. And a promise.

prague_enter.text: Prague. The portal spits you out beneath the old Ossuary Clock, where every gear is wound with bone.
The air tastes of copper. Whatever turns these wheels, it isn't the town council.
Stay close. And watch for movement in the shadows.

wren_meet.text: Easy! Easy, I wasn't stealing it. I was... borrowing it. For a very long time. From a man who's been dead since Tuesday.
You're Wren? The Bell-ringers' street girl?
Ringer's girl, thief's girl, whoever's girl keeps me fed. Look — the Clock took my brother Pavel. Wound him right into the works.
Then we're going the same way.
Good. I know every ledge in this tower. You three just keep swinging and I'll keep us off the floor traps.

prague_gargoyle_hint.text: That statue is warm. Stone shouldn't be warm.
It's a gargoyle shrine. The tower-wardens used to say it'd lend its weight to anyone brave enough to ask.

shrine_gargoyle.text: The gargoyle's eyes ignite — slow, like coals fanned by a patient breath.
You are small. Small things break. Be heavy instead.
Stone settles into Mu's bones. Slower, but unyielding. A strike now carries the weight of a bell.

shrine_gargoyle_after.text: The gargoyle's warmth washes over you. Wounds knit; stone patience holds.

prague_cracked.text: Hear that hollow ring? There's a room behind that wall. Plaster, not stone.
Our blades would only chip it. Something heavier, then.

prague_bars.text: There's a key through those bars. Too narrow for me, and I'd bet Mu can't squeeze through either — unless he travels light.

prague_key.text: You take the Clockmaker's key. It ticks faintly, as though still counting.

prague_locked.text: A brass door, sealed with a keyhole shaped like a gear. It will not budge.

corvin_meet.text: Quiet. Slowly. I've counted the Revenant's footfalls for three weeks and I'd not like to lose count now.
Corvin. I wound the Ossuary Clock for thirty years. Then something older learned its tune and began to wind me.
He's the one who taught my brother the gears!
Pavel? ...The boy's alive. For now. The Revenant keeps what it winds. Take me along — I know the way to its heart.
Girl, I've outlived worse. Lead on.

revenant_defeated.text: The Revenant seizes mid-step. Its great gear unspools, and a thousand silent hours tumble out like dry leaves.
Pavel! ...No. It's only his scarf, wound in the works. He's not here.
He was never here, lass. The Revenant was a trap — a lure for those who'd mend the Bells. Your brother's been taken further east.
Then this is where I turn back, Mu. Tomas lies in Edinburgh, and my mother has no one to light the lamp for her. I need to be there when the thaw comes.
Isolde... you saved me more than once in the vaults.
And you gave me a reason to look up from the ground. Go. Ring the next Bell. I'll keep the lamp lit.
Isolde leaves the party. The second Silent Bell is mended, and a portal of pale light opens.

kelpie_intro.text: The cistern floods without a sound. A shape of black water and weed rises on a horse's neck, a lantern swinging from its bridle.
The Kelpie. Every Scots child is told it: the pale horse at the water's edge that lets you climb on, then never lets you off. It drowned the Nor' Loch's lost for centuries.

golem_intro.text: Dust sifts from the rafters. Rabbi Loew's clay giant stands from its long sleep, a scratched word glowing on its brow.
The Golem of Prague. Made to guard the ghetto, laid to rest in this very attic. Something woke it wrong. It isn't wicked, lass, only confused. Still, it'll flatten us.
The word on its forehead! Remember the old story: take away the first letter and it falls still.

kelpie_defeated.text: The Kelpie shatters into a hundred falling waves. The cistern drains, and the lantern drifts to the stones, still lit.
...Mu. Look at the lantern. The handle's wrapped in my mother's blue thread. That's Tomas's.
He followed that light into the Loch to pull someone out. The Kelpie used him as bait. Even after, he held on to the lantern. Stubborn. Just like me.
Don't be. He's resting now, and the city above has one less ghost in its walls. I'm coming to the next Bell. I want to know what's driving this.
The first Silent Bell is mended. A portal of pale light opens in the cistern.

golem_defeated.text: Wren leaps and scrapes the first letter from the Golem's brow. EMET becomes MET: truth becomes death. The giant crumbles into soft clay.
Pavel! ...No. It's only his scarf, caught in the clay. He's not here.
He was never here, lass. Someone woke the Golem to lure those who'd mend the Bells. Your brother's been taken further east.
Then this is where I turn back, Mu. Tomas lies in Edinburgh, and my mother has no one to light the lamp for her. I need to be there when the thaw comes.
Isolde... you saved me more than once in the vaults.
And you gave me a reason to look up from the ground. Go. Ring the next Bell. I'll keep the lamp lit.
Isolde leaves the party. The second Silent Bell is mended, and a portal of pale light opens.

echo_gate_locked.text: The Echo Gate is sealed. It answers only to a Bell already mended — the last giant must fall first.

strigoi_intro.text: Poenari. They say the prince's wife leapt from these walls rather than be taken. The stones remember more than that.
Those poles... they're all around the hall. Hundreds of them.
A shape unfolds from the throne — tall, gaunt, wings of black velvet. The Strigoi of Poenari lifts its crowned head.
Another warm pulse in my hall. Come. Be a stake, be a story, be nothing.

strigoi_defeated.text: The Strigoi shudders. Its iron crown rings on the flagstones and the stakes crumble to ash.
It was only hunger, wearing a lord's coat.
Hunger's the oldest tyrant, lad. Walk on — the road to Paris is open.
The Echo Gate of Poenari goes quiet. Another glimmers in the chapel.

ankou_intro.text: Bones in the walls, bones in the floor. And someone is counting them.
A cart creaks without a horse. The Ankou, reaper of the Breton dead, turns its hatted skull.
The last to die in the parish drives my cart for a year. Who will take the reins from me, I wonder?

ankou_defeated.text: The scythe clatters to the floor. The cart's wheel stops, and a thousand skulls fall quiet at once.
Death isn't beaten, lad — only reminded to wait.
Then let it wait a long while.
The Ossuary's Echo Gate dims. A gale rises from the north-east.

barghest_intro.text: Whitby. The Black Dog of the cliffs — a Barghest. Sailors swore it presaged a drowning.
Eyes like coals. And it's fast.
Thunder breaks over the ruined abbey. The Barghest rises from the shadows between the arches, hackles smoking with pale fire.

barghest_defeated.text: The Black Dog dissolves into storm-mist, its howl rolling out over the sea.
Wandering omens often are. Come — Venice waits, and she is not as kind as she looks.

plague_intro.text: Il Medico della Peste. The doctors of 1630 wore that mask to keep the miasma out. Venice shut her sick up on islands like this.
It smells of herbs and... something worse.
A beaked giant straightens among the cots, censer swinging. A raven on its shoulder watches you.
Fever is a debt, children. I come to collect.

plague_defeated.text: The Doctor's censer falls, and green smoke thins over the lagoon. The mask cracks — behind it is nothing but herbs and dust.
All that fear, and an empty mask.
Fear fills any mask you hand it, lad. One more road — Rome.

cacus_intro.text: The Aventine. Cacus the fire-breather stole the cattle of Hercules and hid them in his cave, dragging them backward by the tails.
Skulls hang on the cave mouth. Of course they do.
The mountain breathes. A hulking, soot-black giant rises from the smoke, bull horns lashed to his shoulders.
Cattle! Cattle are mine. And so, now, are you.

cacus_defeated.text: Cacus crashes down in a cloud of smoke, the cave shuddering around him. The stolen herd lows somewhere far away.
Five echoes silenced. Five stories finished.
Stories don't finish, lad. They wait for the next teller. Tonight, we'll be it.
The last Echo Gate dims. The road home — and the road onward — is quiet.
